title: Game of Thrones
synopsis: You inherit a castle the size of a wart, on a road every army wants. Two queens want your sword, three gods want your soul, and your maester is out of wine. Welcome to the game.

nodes.text: Two ravens arrive within an hour of each other — one with a Stark direwolf seal, one with a Lannister lion. Both ask the same thing: bend the knee, or burn. Your maester pours the last of the wine and waits.

choices.text: Open the Stark raven first
choices.consequence: The North remembers — and so do its enemies.

choices.text: Open the Lannister raven first
choices.consequence: Gold has a longer reach than honor.

nodes.text: The Stark letter is short and proud — sworn swords, no gold, a place at a council table when the wars are done. Honor like a cold draft through a great hall.

choices.text: Trust the cold honor of the North
choices.consequence: Hard ground holds up the longest.

choices.text: Find it pretty and impractical
choices.consequence: Banners don't feed a garrison.

nodes.text: The Lannister letter rings — a chest of dragons in advance, more after the war, a marriage with a third cousin nobody will miss. Gold has good manners.

choices.text: Take the coin and the comfortable side
choices.consequence: Survival is also a virtue, however cynical.

choices.text: Distrust gold that arrives so cheaply
choices.consequence: A purse this open hides a knife.

nodes.text: Old Maester Edryn has served three lords and outlived two. 'There is no right answer,' he says. 'Only the answer you can live with after.' He coughs. He has, perhaps, a year.

choices.text: Ask him what he would do
choices.consequence: The wise are best asked, not obeyed.

choices.text: Decide alone — the choice is yours
choices.consequence: A lord who borrows backbone has none.

nodes.text: Lady Maren — sharper than your sword and twice as costly — lays out a map at the hearth. 'Hold the river crossing,' she says, 'and both of them will need us.' She does not smile often. She smiles now.

choices.text: Follow her plan to play both sides
choices.consequence: A bridge is the most expensive thing you own.

choices.text: Refuse — call it dishonorable
choices.consequence: Honor is a kind of luxury too.

nodes.text: Your seven small lords gather in the hall. Three are for the Starks, two for the Lannisters, one for declaring himself king of a barn, and one is asleep. Loyalty here is a candle in a draft.

choices.text: Take a vote and abide by it
choices.consequence: Democracy in Westeros is a curiosity.

choices.text: Speak first and tell them where you stand
choices.consequence: Lords lead. Bannermen follow or leave.

nodes.text: A merchant claims he saw a shadow with wings the size of a longship pass over the Narrow Sea. A child claims the same. The maester scoffs and does not sleep that night.

choices.text: Send a man east to confirm
choices.consequence: Knowledge is the only armor that fits everyone.

choices.text: Dismiss it as a rumor and a child
choices.consequence: Dragons are stories. Until they aren't.

nodes.text: A column of mercenaries crosses your river in the night. By dawn there are dead men in the reeds — three of theirs, one of yours, a boy of fifteen who liked the cook's daughter. The war has arrived without asking.

choices.text: Hang the prisoners as a warning
choices.consequence: Cruelty travels fast and ugly.

choices.text: Send them home with bread and a message
choices.consequence: Mercy can be a kind of edge.

nodes.text: A line of strangers from the North — gaunt, frostbitten, refugees from things worse than men — wait at your gates. The septon calls them savages. The cook offers them broth.

choices.text: Take them in and use their strong backs
choices.consequence: Allies arrive in odd skins.

choices.text: Turn them away to spare your stores
choices.consequence: A castle that feeds everyone feeds no one.

nodes.text: Your steward is caught passing word to the Lannisters. He has six children. The law is clear; the law is also a heavy weight to carry. Maren wants him beheaded by sundown.

choices.text: Execute him publicly to keep order
choices.consequence: Iron speaks plainly.

choices.text: Spare him and use him as a false-message conduit
choices.consequence: A turned spy is sharper than any blade.

nodes.text: Maren discovers a Lannister man in the scullery — leaving for two months, learning the tunnels. He kneels and begs and his accent is from a village two valleys over.

choices.text: Quietly disappear the spy
choices.consequence: Some problems vanish best at night.

choices.text: Feed him a beautiful lie and let him 'escape'
choices.consequence: Information aimed back is the cheapest weapon.

nodes.text: An invitation arrives, stamped with the Frey star and weighted with too much ceremony. A wedding. Both sides will be there. Maester Edryn has gone very still.

choices.text: Attend — refusal is its own statement
choices.consequence: The most dangerous rooms are the most necessary.

choices.text: Send your regrets and an honest gift
choices.consequence: Some doors are closed for the body and opened for the soul.

nodes.text: The septon preaches that war is a punishment from the Seven for lords forgetting the small folk. Your peasants nod. So do, awkwardly, two of your bannermen. A sermon is sometimes the start of a politics.

choices.text: Embrace him publicly to win the smallfolk
choices.consequence: A god on your side travels free.

choices.text: Quietly muzzle him before he becomes a movement
choices.consequence: Sermons can outrun swords.

nodes.text: You ride in under your banner with a small honor guard. The hall is too full, the music is too loud, and the wine is too generous. You see Maren count exits three times.

choices.text: Leave before the toast
choices.consequence: Trust her counting.

choices.text: Stay and hold your position
choices.consequence: A lord who flees a wedding becomes a story.

nodes.text: Instead you broker a marriage of your own — your eldest to a neutral house with a tower of grain and no taste for war. Maren writes the contract; the maester signs as witness; nobody is in love. It is, by Westerosi standards, a love story.

choices.text: Make the pact public and binding
choices.consequence: Allies welded in candle-wax.

choices.text: Keep it secret until the war declares a winner
choices.consequence: A card is sharpest when it is still face-down.

nodes.text: An army arrives — whichever army you betrayed, or didn't — and rings your walls. Inside there is food for forty days, a maester with a fever, and Maren saying, far too calmly, that she's been preparing for this her whole life.

choices.text: Hold the siege to the last grain
choices.consequence: Walls win wars patient men forget.

choices.text: Negotiate from strength while you still can
choices.consequence: Speak first, before hunger does.

nodes.text: On a hill between camps you meet a rival lord and a flagon of wine and a sky full of indifferent stars. Treaties under stars never quite hold to morning, but they are, sometimes, where wars actually end.

choices.text: Swear the treaty and mean it
choices.consequence: Honor offered first is harder to refuse.

choices.text: Swear it and plan to break it cleverly
choices.consequence: Cleverness comes due, eventually.

nodes.text: A shape passes over your towers, and the temperature drops, and your archers forget what their bows are for. The dragon is real. The dragon has noticed you. The world tilts.

choices.text: Kneel to whoever rides the dragon
choices.consequence: Some powers you bow to without shame.

choices.text: Hide your house from the dragon's gaze
choices.consequence: Be small enough to escape notice.

nodes.text: Word comes from the North that is worse than dragons — that the dead walk, that the Wall has fallen, that whatever color of king sits at King's Landing will not matter when winter actually arrives.

choices.text: Ride north with all your spears
choices.consequence: Some causes outrank a throne.

choices.text: Fortify south and let the kingdoms cope
choices.consequence: Charity that ruins you helps no one.

nodes.text: A new ruler — whoever survived the wedding, the siege, and the dragon — summons you to court. The summons is silk-wrapped. You know what silk-wrapped summons mean.

choices.text: Attend court and play the long game
choices.consequence: The game of thrones is for those who like rooms.

choices.text: Refuse and rule your small corner well
choices.consequence: Wisdom is also a kind of crown.

nodes.text: You stand on your battlements at dawn and look out at the world you outlived. Maren joins you with two cups of cooling tea. The realm is full of corpses and kings. You and yours are still here.

choices.text: Decide to ride out and build a kingdom of your own
choices.consequence: Small lords can become large ones, given time and luck.

choices.text: Decide enough is enough and live
choices.consequence: Some victories taste like an ordinary morning.

choices.text: Burn what you cannot defend before the dragon comes
choices.consequence: There is dignity even in ash.

nodes.text: Years later, in a hall hung with the banners of three dead houses, men call you Lord Paramount and bow lower than they used to. You did not start the game. You merely outlived everyone who did. Maren, beside you, hides a smile that has waited a decade.

Wars end. Kings die. Your river keeps running. You spend your old age in a hall warm with grandchildren and one fat dog, telling stories to people who don't quite believe how close you came to mattering. You laugh. They were the lucky ones.

When winter truly comes you ride north with what you have. Most of you do not return. Songs are sung about you in the long halls of houses you never knew existed. It is a small kind of immortality, but a real one.
